notes: Ran into the known IP Block about 27 times with no breaker or link, and twice used Stimhack into it, taking core damage for nothing. It never installed anything after turn 1 and spent the late game clicking for credits to remove tags while the Corp scored freely.
Scored steadily behind Resistor and fast-advanced Breaking News in remotes. Minor oddities were icing an empty remote on turn 1 and putting late ice on Archives.

Ran unprotected R&D 3-4 times a turn, which mostly re-accessed the same top card. From turn 7 on it only clicked for credits, sitting on 23 credits with nothing installed while the Corp advanced and scored agendas in remotes it never contested.
Snare trap, then a sensible rebuild with Melange and Hedge Funds and scoring out of a well-iced remote. Posted Bounty was stolen through two ice by a rich Runner, and it drew 2 into a discard once.

Good early economy plus Mining Accident, then steady R&D pressure won the game. Minor issues were sitting on many tags, a low-credit facecheck on HQ, and using Stimhack (core damage) on a run that didn't need it.

A decent start (GFI, Oaktown, Atlas scored) gave way to a broke stall: over 11 turns it paid its last credits to trash a Crowdfunding that kept coming back, and it threw away its hand with Audacity. It never installed or scored again, and HQ and R&D were held only by Data Ravens, which let runs through.

Reasonable setup and a good steal of Private Security Force, but it took a Shadow tag on the last click and ended the turn tagged with a 3-card grip against Weyland. Scorched Earth then flatlined it, which running earlier in the turn would have avoided.

Installed Atman at strength 0, then ran open R&D repeatedly, seeing the same card. After bouncing off Viper and Enigma it sat clicking for credits up to 32 without installing a breaker while the Corp scored out of those remotes.

Spent turns 2-7 clicking for credits at 10-18 credits with a full hand, discarding every turn, and two discarded agendas were stolen from unprotected Archives. The later play was solid: a 3-ice remote scoring Accelerated Beta Tests.
Scored two SDS behind a single ice efficiently, but left R&D unprotected for seven turns of 4-run digs, giving up SSL Endorsement. It also clicked for credits while discarding.
Efficient economy and scoring out of a Resistor remote. The only issues were stockpiling 25+ credits and drawing into discards.

Strong early steals and a good rig (Paperclip, Black Orchestra, Consume), ending with a well-timed remote steal. Oddities: it spent 12 credits breaking Mausolus and then jacked out, and used Stimhack on runs that didn't need it, taking core damage.

Never installed an agenda: it clicked for credits up to 19 while discarding every turn, and played Psychographics with no tags. Its late plan was trashing Liberated Accounts, Bellona sat in an HQ with one ice and was stolen, and the 4 Hard-Hitting News tags were never punished.

Ran unprotected HQ four times a turn, mostly re-accessing the same known cards. It never once ran the single-ice remote where the Corp advanced and scored three agendas, including GFI left advanced overnight.

Won through R&D/HQ access, but repeatedly let a known Cobra fire (losing Cloak, Corroder, Houdini and Switchblade plus cards) while holding Switchblade and money. It also sat on tags and paid Data Ward every run.

Clicked for credits while rich and discarding every turn, then used Consulting Visit into Audacity to trash its whole hand into an unprotected Archives. The Runner took three agendas from Archives and won on turn 5.

A strong Account Siphon opening, efficient R&D runs through Resistor, and a good Data Leak Reversal mill into Archives. The minor waste was paying to clear Joshua B. tags that cost nothing against a broke Corp.

Built a 4-ice remote on turns 3-8 and never installed an agenda in it all game. For about 30 turns it mostly clicked for credits up to 32 and discarded while the Runner dug R&D, and it never scored a point.
Good drip economy and a Biotic Labor fast-advance for Beale, then scored behind Tollbooth. Hard-Hitting News had no follow-up, but the tags still taxed the Runner.

Wasted turn 1 re-running open R&D, then spent almost all its money removing tags and installed no breakers until turn 13. It stole one GFI through Mausolus but never contested the remote where the winning GFI was advanced over three turns.
